rationale: The Latin anchors *persistere* ("to persist, persevere") and *instare* ("to press on, urge") both convey active, determined continuation — as confirmed by the context "ut in fide veritatis persisterent semper ac proficerent" (that they might always persist and advance in the faith of truth) and "illi instabant" (they kept pressing/insisting). This points to the volitional sense of refusing to stop (persevere.v.01) rather than mere passive continuance (prevail.v.03) or physical staying behind (persist.v.03).
